title: Leverage, win-win and the drip
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Where does your leverage in a deal come from?

A student said: leverage is negotiating power, who has the ability to walk away. It is the most important thing in any deal; you may not have the upper hand, but find as much leverage as you can, because that gives you control.
Another said that the best leverage is bringing value, though when you do not have value, leverage can be forced.
Jose said that his rule is: I only do deals that are win-win, and that the biggest challenge is at the very beginning.

Jose said that the author talks about creating omnipresence while building your brand: you are not a flash in the pan, you get steady momentum over time. Use the drip: always publish a little article.
A student said that he repeats the same values in a podcast so the people who come through are already filtered by the time they meet him.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write your leverage in your next deal.
Write the win for them and the win for you.
Write what you will publish every week.
Write your values in one line.

check.q: What did a student say leverage is?
What did Jose say his rule is?
What did Jose say the drip is?

recap: Find leverage. Make it win-win. Keep dripping.
